title: On-call & Incident Response: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status and Comms Templates
author: Asha Patel
summary: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices into a single, actionable reference. It covers incident classification and lifecycle, runbook templates and examples, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation and escalation policies, game-day planning, and ready-to-use status page and customer communication templates. Use this page as the canonical operational standard for all sev-impacts affecting production inference services.
incident_process:
Purpose:
- Provide a single reference for triage, escalation, mitigation, and communications during incidents affecting production inference, dedicated pools, or customer-private deployments.

Severity taxonomy and SLAs:
1) Sev1 (Critical)
   - Criteria: Customer-visible outage or severe degradation across multiple regions or loss of inference request routing (e.g., 50%+ request errors, universal 503/504).
   - Immediate action: page primary on-call, notify on-call lead.
   - Response SLA: Acknowledge and begin mitigation within 15 minutes.
   - Communication cadence: initial ack within 30 minutes, updates every 30 minutes until stabilized.

2) Sev2 (Major)
   - Criteria: Degraded performance affecting a subset of customers or significant QoS regression (latency > 2x SLO, elevated error rates for a single service).
   - Immediate action: page primary, inform secondary if unresolved after 30 minutes.
   - Response SLA: Acknowledge within 30 minutes.
   - Communication cadence: updates every 60 minutes.

3) Sev3 (Minor)
   - Criteria: Low-impact incidents, single-customer non-blocking issues, or internal alerts that do not significantly affect customer experience.
   - Immediate action: log ticket and assign to team during working hours.
   - Response SLA: Acknowledge within 8 business hours.

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection and Triage
   - Automated alerts, customer reports, or SRE monitoring trigger a triage.
   - Primary on-call runs initial checks from the detection checklist and determines severity.
2) Mitigation
   - Execute runbook(s) for the affected subsystem. If no runbook exists, follow the generic mitigation checklist below.
3) Escalation
   - If unresolved within the severity SLA, escalate to secondary, then to on-call lead, then to engineering manager and PL. Use the escalation matrix in the oncall_rotations section.
4) Communication
   - Post initial ack, publish status page entry and send customer comms per templates.
5) Recovery and Validation
   - Confirm full service restoration, validate with synthetic checks and 3 affected customers (if applicable).
6) Post-incident
   - Open a postmortem within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev2, assign owners and remediation dates.

Generic initial mitigation checklist (use before/while running a runbook):
- Collect context: alert IDs, timestamps, scope, affected regions, last deploys.
- Check service health dashboards and recent deploys (last 60 minutes).
- Run specific smoke tests and synthetic traces.
- If traffic spike suspected, engage traffic shaping or fallback routing.
- If resource saturation suspected, apply autoscaling or temporarily increase capacity if SRE approves.
- Preserve logs and take memory/CPU snapshots for postmortem.
- Do not perform risky rollbacks without manager approval for production-critical models.
runbooks:
This section contains example runbooks and a template to use when creating new runbooks. Every runbook must include owner, pre-reqs, safe mitigation steps, verification steps, rollback criteria, and post-incident notes.

Runbook template (required fields):
- title
- owner (team and alias)
- severity applicability
- prerequisites and access (dashboards, runbook links, playbooks)
- detection steps (alerts/metrics to confirm)
- step-by-step mitigation with CLI/commands where applicable
- verification steps and acceptance criteria
- rollback and emergency-stop criteria
- post-incident data capture checklist

Example runbook: Model-serving 503 spike (primary API gateway returns 503 to customers)
- owner: eng-serving-runtime oncall (primary)
- severity: Sev1/Sev2 depending on scope
- prerequisites: access to kubectl cluster-redwood-prod, gateway logs (ELK), routing console, capacity dashboard

Detection:
1) Alert: api.gateway.503_rate > 5% sustained for 2 minutes OR customer reports multiple 503s.
2) Confirm: curl -I https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
   - expect HTTP 200 and body 'ok' for healthy services.

Mitigation steps:
1) Identify scope: check routing region and model variant: kubectl get pods -n inference -l service=gateway -o wide
2) If gateway pods are OOM or CrashLoopBackOff: kubectl logs -n inference <pod> --tail=200; scale up gateway: kubectl scale deploy/gateway --replicas=6 -n inference
3) If downstream model-serving workers are saturated: check worker queues and KV cache hit rate. If queue length > 1000 and CPU>80%, route traffic to fallback model variant: update routing rule in routing console to route 20% to fallback model (document change and notify).
4) If the issue correlates with a recent deploy within last 60 minutes: consider rolling back the deploy for the affected service after manager approval: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> -n inference
5) When making config or routing changes, record the exact change in the incident channel and add to the timeline.

Verification:
- Verify 503 rate drops to <0.5% for 15 minutes, and synthetic requests succeed from 3 regions.
- Validate downstream model latencies within SLO for 10 consecutive minutes.

Rollback criteria (stop mitigation and rollback change):
- If customer impact increases after mitigation step or new errors appear.
- If metrics do not improve after two mitigation steps, escalate.

For platform teams: keep runbooks concise and keep the commands copy-paste ready. Each runbook must include an owner and be reviewed annually.
oncall_rotations:
Rotation model and responsibilities:
- Primary on-call: first responder for alerts and customer-impacting incidents. Expected to perform triage, initial mitigation, and communications.
- Secondary on-call: backup for primary; handles escalations if primary is overloaded or unresolved after severity SLA.
- On-call lead: coordinates cross-team efforts for Sev1 and high-impact Sev2s, authorizes emergency capacity changes, and approves customer-facing communications.
- Pager duty schedule: weekly rotation by default, with exceptions for engineering managers and long-term coverage.

Escalation matrix (time-based):
- Sev1: page primary -> if no ack in 15 minutes, page secondary -> if unresolved after 30 minutes, page on-call lead -> if unresolved after 60 minutes, escalate to EM and Product Lead.
- Sev2: page primary -> if no ack in 30 minutes, page secondary and inform on-call lead.
- Sev3: create ticket and assign to owning team during business hours.

Handoff checklist (for rotation changes and shift handoff):
1) Confirm current incidents and their state.
2) Summarize open actions and owners.
3) Share temporary credentials or runbook pointers if required.
4) Confirm receipt of handoff in Slack oncall-channel with timestamp.

On-call best practices and fatigue management:
- Limit pager exposure by routing low-urgency alerts to the team queue.
- Use predictable weekly rotations and allow 1 swap per quarter without managerial approval.
- If on-call spans a vacation or extended absence, update schedule and reassign at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Keep a personal playbook of debugging shortcuts and links to runbooks.
game_days:
Purpose and scope:
- Game days are scheduled exercises to validate runbooks, on-call coordination, and platform resiliency. They should include both planned simulations and surprise 'fire drill' variants.

Planning checklist for a game day:
1) Objective: define 2-3 specific goals (e.g., validate failover to fallback model, test autoscaling under load, confirm communications pipeline).
2) Scope: choose affected services and regions, define blast radius, and get approvals from service owners.
3) Participants: primary/secondary on-call, on-call lead, product owner, SRE, and at least one developer from each affected service.
4) Pre-game validation: take snapshots of dashboards and confirm backups.
5) Schedule: announce game day to internal teams at least 1 week in advance; keep one 'surprise' drill per quarter.

Sample game day scenario: Degraded KV cache causes 2x model latency in eu-west-1
- Inject fault: throttle cache responses for 5 minutes in the staging environment and observe failover behavior.
- Validate: run synthetic traffic that mimics 99th percentile sequence lengths and observe latency and cost changes.
- Success criteria: automated fallback triggers within 120 seconds, latency returns to <1.5x SLO for 95% of requests, and no customer-visible errors.

Post-game tasks:
- Run a retro within 48 hours, capture lessons learned, update runbooks, and assign owners for remediation.
- Publish a short game day summary on the internal engineering wiki and mark runbooks updated.
status_page_and_comms_templates:
Status page and customer communications are critical to maintain trust during incidents. Below are templates for status page entries and customer email updates. Keep language clear, non-technical, and avoid speculative causes.

Status page template (short-form):
- Title: Degraded inference latency in eu-west-1
- Impact: Some users may experience increased latency or higher error rates when calling hosted inference endpoints in eu-west-1.
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
- Started: 2026-02-14T14:10:00Z
- Next update: 30 minutes
- More info: link to incident channel and postmortem (when available)

Customer email template - initial acknowledgement:
- Subject: Redwood Inference - Incident affecting inference latency in eu-west-1
- Body: Hello,

We are investigating an issue impacting inference latency for some requests routed through our eu-west-1 region. Our on-call team is actively triaging the cause and working on mitigation. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

If you are experiencing critical business impact, please reply to this message with details and we will prioritize accordingly.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Operations Team

Customer email template - update:
- Subject: Update - Redwood Inference incident (eu-west-1)
- Body: Hello,

Update: Our team has identified that the issue is related to increased load on the KV cache layer which caused elevated model latency. We have applied a temporary routing change to shift 30% of traffic to a fallback model variant and have restored acceptable latency for the majority of affected requests.

Next steps: We are continuing to monitor and will provide a further update in 60 minutes or when there is a significant change.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Operations Team

Customer email template - resolved:
- Subject: Resolved - Redwood Inference incident (eu-west-1)
- Body: Hello,

The incident affecting inference latency in eu-west-1 has been resolved. All services are operating normally and we have reverted temporary routing changes. We will publish a post-incident report detailing the root cause and remediation plan within 3 business days.

We apologize for the impact and thank you for your patience.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Operations Team
postmortem_template:
Postmortem template (use for Sev1 and Sev2 incidents)
- title
- incident_id
- severity
- incident_owner
- date & timeline (ordered list of events with timestamps)
- summary (one-paragraph impact statement)
- scope and customer impact (affected customers, duration, SLO misses)
- root cause analysis (write causal chain; include technical evidence and logs)
- contributing factors (process, monitoring gaps, rollout issues)
- mitigation and remediation (short-term fixes and long-term actions with owners and due dates)
- verification plan (how we will validate the remediation)
- lessons learned and runbook updates (list runbooks updated with links)
- follow-up review date and attendees

Postmortem expectations and SLAs:
- Sev1: postmortem draft within 72 hours; final report and remediation owners assigned within 7 days.
- Sev2: postmortem draft within 7 days.
- All postmortems should include an annotated timeline and at least one quantitative graph demonstrating the impact (error rate, latency percentiles, traffic).
notes:
Ownership and governance:
- The eng-sre and eng-serving-runtime teams share ownership for incident process and runbooks.
- All service owners must keep runbooks current and review them annually.
- The incident process and templates will be reviewed quarterly by SRE and engineering leadership.

Contact and escalation aliases:
- Pager alias: oncall-primary@redwood-inference.com
- Slack channel: #oncall-incidents
- Incident Zoom: zoom.us/j/XXXXXXXX (use the incident channel to request and lock the meeting)
